intro: Every UK employer must carry out right to work checks before someone starts work. We help you set up a simple, compliant process, so you avoid civil penalties and protect your business.
cardText: Checking every employee’s right to work, the right way.

checklist.hint: Manual, online share code or digital ID

purposes.title: Manual document check
purposes.text: For British and Irish passports and some other documents.

purposes.title: Online share code check
purposes.text: For people with an eVisa or settled status.

purposes.title: Digital identity check
purposes.text: Through a certified provider, for valid British and Irish passports.

Accepting a document that isn’t on the Home Office list
Missing a follow-up check when permission expires

rules.title: Civil penalties
rules.text: Employing someone who doesn’t have the right to work can lead to a penalty of up to £45,000 per worker for a first breach, and £60,000 for repeat breaches.

rules.title: eVisas have replaced most physical documents
rules.text: Most migrants now prove their status online with a share code instead of a BRP.

rules.title: Sponsors have extra duties
rules.text: Right to work checks are part of your [sponsor licence compliance](/sponsor-licence-compliance/).

boxTitle: Want a second pair of eyes before you apply?
boxText: A consultation costs far less than a refused application. We’ll check your case against the current rules and tell you honestly where you stand.

sections.heading: How to carry out right to work checks
sections.text: Ask to see the employee’s original documents in their presence, or use the Home Office online checking service with their share code, or a certified digital identity provider for British and Irish passports. Check the documents are genuine and belong to them, make a clear dated copy, and keep it securely.

faqs.q: Do I need to check British employees?
faqs.a: Yes. Right to work checks apply to everyone you employ, so you have a defence against a penalty.
A code the employee gets from GOV.UK that lets you check their right to work online.

faqs.q: How long must I keep the records?
faqs.a: For the time the person works for you, and for 2 years after they leave.
